A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the bed expansion of a down-flow fluidized-bed reactor can be described by the Richardson-Zaki equation, when the terminal velocity and the expansion coefficient are determined from the experimental bed expansion data.
the terminal velocity of a particle can be determined from bed expansion characteristics.

The main takeaway from our work is that

the drag coefficient for free-rising particles in an anaerobic down-flow fluidized bed reactor is lower than that of a standard drag curve (Karamanevs and Nikolov,1992a,b), and that it depends on biofilm thickness.
the drag coefficient of particles in a down-flow fluidized bed is not only dependent of the Reynolds number but also on the biofilm thickness and the particle density.
, for the same particle density, the drag force acting on a particle increases with increasing biofilm thickness.
